subject.title: [Feature]: Intelligent Model Fallback with Wildcard/Auto Selection

question: Which public provider-family fallback contract should OpenClaw support here: wildcard/auto refs, explicit fallbackFamilies groups, catalog-derived fallbacks, or no new core fallback contract for now?
rationale: This changes public config and provider-routing behavior, and repository policy treats fallback and config surface additions as product-sensitive rather than a routine repair.

options.title: Choose one core fallback contract
options.body: Pick one canonical config/runtime shape and require implementation across schema, resolver, embedded fallback gates, docs, and migration/doctor expectations.

options.title: Use plugin routing only
options.body: Keep core fallbacks flat and direct provider-family policies to before_model_resolve plugins, accepting that this will not express ordered failure-chain semantics natively.

options.title: Defer the surface
options.body: Leave explicit fallbacks as the only supported contract until stronger user evidence or a maintainer-sponsored design narrows the behavior.

recommendation.title: Choose one core fallback contract
recommendation.body: Pick one canonical config/runtime shape and require implementation across schema, resolver, embedded fallback gates, docs, and migration/doctor expectations.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current and historical signal on model fallback resolution and the related product-sensitive failover paths.
